record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: geometric proof and sharp constant for a degree estimate
record.original_question: For continuous maps f: S^1 -> S^1, Theorem 5.2 gives an estimate of |deg f| by a nonlocal integral over pairs (x,y) for which |f(x)-f(y)| >= sqrt(3). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of this estimate? What is the best possible constant C in that estimate, and is the best constant achieved by some map?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.2 ([26, Open Problem 18]). Is there a simpler, more geometric proof of Theorem 5.2? What is the best constant C in (5.3)? Is it achieved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ denote the unit circle equipped with arclength measure, and let $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ denote the topological (Brouwer) degree of a continuous map $f : S^1 \to S^1$. There exists a finite constant $C > 0$ such that, for every continuous $f : S^1 \to S^1$,
$$|\deg f| \;\le\; C \iint_{\{(x,y)\in S^1\times S^1 \,:\, |f(x)-f(y)| \ge \sqrt{3}\,\}} \frac{1}{|x-y|^{2}}\, d\mathcal{H}^1(x)\, d\mathcal{H}^1(y), \qquad (*)$$
where $|f(x)-f(y)|$ denotes Euclidean distance in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the threshold $\sqrt{3}$ is the chord length corresponding to an arc of $2\pi/3$ on $S^1$.

Address the following three questions:

(a) Provide a simpler, more geometric proof of inequality $(*)$ than the existing analytic proofs.

(b) Determine the best (smallest) admissible constant $C$ in $(*)$.

(c) Decide whether this best constant is attained, that is, whether there exists a continuous map $f : S^1 \to S^1$ for which equality holds in $(*)$ with $C$ replaced by the optimal constant.
artifact.status_search_result: The inequality belongs to the family of Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen degree estimates. Refinements have been obtained for higher-dimensional spheres, and a recent preprint of F. Hernández (2022) makes progress "towards a refined estimate" in the one-dimensional case, but no published source identifies the sharp constant in the S¹ → S¹ estimate with threshold √3 nor exhibits an extremal map; a purely geometric proof of the estimate is also not reported. The sharp-constant and attainment questions appear to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Towards a refined estimate for topological degree in one dimension
status_evidence.snippet: we prove an inequality inspired by a conjecture of Brezis, which asks for a bound for the topological degree of a map from the circle to itself in terms of a nonlocal integral.
status_evidence.claim: The S¹ case of the Brezis-type degree estimate is still being refined; sharp constant is not established.

status_evidence.title: A refined estimate for the topological degree
status_evidence.snippet: refinement of the Bourgain–Brezis–Nguyen estimate for the topological degree of continuous maps from a sphere into itself for d ≥ 2
status_evidence.claim: Refinements exist for d ≥ 2; the d = 1 (circle) case remained open.

status_evidence.title: New Questions Related to the Topological Degree (Brezis)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on degree estimates including best constants in nonlocal integral bounds for circle maps.
status_evidence.claim: Brezis lists the best-constant question for the circle estimate as an open problem.
